definitions.explanation: A structure for containing fire, used for heating, cooking, or industrial processes. Ranges from traditional sunken hearths ({囲炉裏|いろり}) in Japanese homes to industrial furnaces and nuclear reactors.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{民家|みんか}→民家：13217_minka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{囲炉裏|いろり}→囲炉裏：12008_irori⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれる→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧{炉|ろ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Old folk houses have a hearth called an irori.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{製鉄所|せいてつじょ}→製鉄所：25282_seitetsujo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{溶鉱炉|ようこうろ}→溶鉱炉：23628_youkouro⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一日|いちにち}→一日：00942_ichinichi⟧{二十四時間|にじゅうよじかん}⟦{稼働|かどう}して→稼働する：19633_kadousuru⟧おり、⟦{鉄|てつ}→鉄：02225_tetsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{溶|と}かし→溶かす：08264_tokasu⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: The blast furnace at this steelworks operates 24 hours a day, continuously melting iron.

notes:
USAGE:
Appears in many compounds related to heating and industrial processes. In tea ceremony, {炉|ろ} refers to the sunken hearth cut into the tatami floor, used during the cold months (November to April) as opposed to the portable brazier ({風炉|ふろ}) used in warmer months.

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{囲炉裏|いろり}→囲炉裏：12008_irori⟧: traditional sunken hearth
- ⟦{溶鉱炉|ようこうろ}→溶鉱炉：23628_youkouro⟧: blast furnace
- ⟦{原子炉|げんしろ}→原子炉：20824_genshiro⟧: nuclear reactor
- ⟦{暖炉|だんろ}→暖炉：18480_danro⟧: fireplace
- {風炉|ふろ}: portable brazier (tea ceremony)
